the_signal.headline: Self-hosted LLMs kill token arbitrage—your margin problem just changed
the_signal.body: n8n's analysis surfaces what's been inevitable: current token pricing is subsidized and unsustainable. GTM teams relying on API pricing models need to stress-test their unit economics now against self-hosted alternatives. The cost structure of your AI revenue system will flip when market rates reflect real compute.

tool_drop.name: Deltix
tool_drop.what: AI-driven testing platform that automates test case generation and validation for software workflows.
tool_drop.why: If your revenue system runs on agents and workflows (n8n, MCP, Claude Code), AI-native testing becomes your bottleneck—Deltix closes the gap between agent deployment speed and test coverage reliability.

thread_of_day.title: RPA vs. Workflow Automation: Building Automation That Lasts
thread_of_day.takeaway: Workflow automation wins on observability, scalability, and governance—RPA breaks at enterprise scale because you can't see inside the black box when it fails.

quote.text: We don't know how much a token really costs. They are subsidized by big tech and most AI providers are operating at a loss.
quote.source: n8n Blog - Token prices won't increase if you host your own LLMs

whats_moving.context: Token subsidy model breaking forces GTM teams to recalculate per-call costs; on-prem deployments suddenly look cheaper at scale.
n8n's multi-part series on deployment patterns signals market shift toward self-hosted, auditable automation over black-box RPA.
Deltix and broader HN conversation on AI testing emergence—teams shipping agents faster now need equivalent speed in QA.

act_on_this: Run a token cost comparison: calculate your current API spend vs. a self-hosted Claude or Llama deployment at your actual usage volume. Lock in results before Q4 pricing changes hit.

numbers.context: Agent integration surface area has exploded; your bottleneck is no longer 'can I plug in X service' but 'can I observe and debug what happens inside the agent when X fails.'
